verdicts.reason: HELD, verified line-for-line in the web payload. §1t99s0§.as:3050 is exactly 'return this.§1t4469s0§() && this.§1t4414s0§ >= 48;' and :3060 is exactly 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ < 48)' + 'return;'. :3058-3081 is a four-branch cycler -1->§1t12220s0§, 12220->12221, 12221->12222, 12222->12220, then pushes to §1t251s0§. The constants at :27,:29,:31 are 0/1/2, and the android twin names them LIGHT_STANCE=0 / BALANCED_STANCE=1 / HEAVY_STANCE=2 (MCSPlayer.as:27,29,31), so the light->balanced->heavy->light ordering is right. grep for §1t4472s0§ over the whole payload returns exactly the two callers claimed: the battle-HUD handler §1t5207s0§ at §1t113s0§.as:468-479 (Snd_smallClick on pass, Snd_error on refusal) and Keyboard.SPACE at §1t1541s0§.as:605-611. §1t113s0§ is the battle HUD (its :117 getString(45)='Hit Combo', :121 getString(175)='Critical Hit', and its §1t5208s0§ stance-colour setter is the positional twin of android BattleUI.setStanceColor). I then went past the claim and opened the artifact the ledger itself rests on: §1t113s0§.as:326-359 maps the third HUD bar as (reload-48)/(maxreload-48) and shows a grey getString(960) label ONLY when that value is 0, hides it while 0<fill<1, and swaps to black getString(175) 'Critical Hit' at fill>=1. Frame reference/frames/duel_dense/Nr4fQstqHDM_428.0.png shows that third bar EMPTY with 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' on it; frame reference/frames/duel_frames/Nr4fQstqHDM_t435.0s.png, same fighter and same run seven seconds later, shows the bar ~40% filled and the label GONE. The frame and the code agree, so no frame-vs-doc conflict arises here; what falls is the ledger's INFERENCE from the frame. Residual defect is minor only: the finding's lane_impact says 'gated reload >= 48' without noting that maxreload is itself 48 + SPD*6 (§1t1523s0§.as:2276), so 48 is the meter's floor, not a fraction of it.

HUNTER CAVEAT that keeps this at 'minor': the finding's HEADLINE artifact is v0.682 (android GameEngine), and under the S0-3 parity caveat an android UI string alone cannot settle web v0.717 behaviour — the overturn actually rests on the second half of its own cite, the web SPACE handler and the web gate. verdicts.reason:
HELD, and the quote citeLint could not locate is real — it just spans a binary blob with CRLF, which is why the linter said QUOTE_UNVERIFIED. My own decode finds at byte offset 434948 exactly '<anim i="deathnohead" d="31">
<f i="0">
<n i="16" x="-18" y="-88" r="-83"></n>
<n i="20" x="-18" y="-61" r="-104"></n>' — character for character what the finding quoted. Measured myself: the file holds 158 <anim> roots (matching S0-4), the deathnohead block holds 31 <f> frames and 399 <n> records, and the death family is exactly death/deathenemy/deathnohand/deathnohead/deathwitharrow/deathbyarrow/deathdowned/deathinhalf. The web-vs-android identity is NOT the circular C2 diff: 108_1t4635s0.bin carries the obfuscated web symbol name and is indexed as a web bindata file, so md5 equality here is genuine cross-build parity evidence rather than a file compared with itself. RESIDUAL DEFECT (minor, and it is why severity is not clean): 'each carrying about seventeen node records' is true for frames 0-22 only; frames 23-30 carry ONE node each (always node 16). The finding's 'nothing left to catalogue' is therefore slightly hot — the bone track is complete, but the node-index-to-limb-sprite mapping is not in this blob.

HELD on every line number it gives. §1t1523s0§.as:2638 opens §1t9600s0§ (the rebirth routine); :2644 is 'if(§1t7356s0§(§1t9426s0§) == 8)', :2646 '§1t9713s0§(§1t9413s0§,100);', :2651 '§1t9713s0§(§1t9413s0§,25);', :2653 'if(§1t7356s0§(§1t9426s0§) < 9)'. I resolved the two ids myself instead of taking them on trust: §1t1523s0§.as:228 '§1t9413s0§:int = 12' and :254 '§1t9426s0§:int = 25', against android StatsManager.as:194 'STAT_HGOLD:int = 12' and :220 'STAT_DAN:int = 25'. The android twin doRebirth is at StatsManager.as:2195 with the 20/5 pair at :2203/:2207 and the same '< 9' cap at :2209, so the 25/100 pair really is a v0.717-specific datum. RR:164-165 therefore falls whole: dan is hard-capped at 9 (displayed +1 = ten rungs), so MAX_DAN_RANK=10 is CONTRACT from web source, and the dan==8 branch paying 100 hard gold is precisely the '10th-rebirth tier' the ledger says does not exist. The minor defect is in the lane_impact, not the overturn: the dan titles are strings 455-464, not 456-464 — 455 is '(初段)', so it is ten ids for ten rungs, and a rewrite that copies '456-464' would ship a nine-rung ladder.

HELD, and the id resolution I did myself is what makes it safe. §1t5957s0§.as:3340 is 'var _loc2_:int = §1t1523s0§.§1t9714s0§(§1t1523s0§.§1t9411s0§);' and :3341-3346 are the six add-button visibility gates. From §1t1523s0§.as:206-234 the ids are §1t9403s0§=1, §1t9406s0§=4, §1t9408s0§=6, §1t9409s0§=7, §1t9410s0§=8, §1t9411s0§=10, §1t9415s0§=14, which against android StatsManager.as:170-200 are exactly MAXHP / MAXCHI / ATTACK / DEFENSE / SPEED / LEVEL / MAXAP — the six gates line up one-for-one with android InventoryUI.as:2407-2412 in the same order. So the formulas are real: ATK/DEF/SPD < 1+(lvl+10)*3, MAXHP < 10+(lvl+10)*10, MAXCHI < 10+(lvl+10)*5, MAXAP < 30+(lvl+10)*5. At the level cap of 80 that is 271 / 910 / 460 / 480, and android's coefficients (lvl+10, 10+(lvl+10)*5, 20+(lvl+10)) give 90, not 271 — second confirmation it is a web datum. RR:201's 'gear/rebirth-inclusive' explanation is false: 271 is a pure level function on the base stat and gear never enters it. HUNTER NOTE (why severity is minor, not clean): the finding says the ledger's arithmetic 'is answering a question the code never asked', but the parenthetical '(237-point first-run budget makes it impossible in one stat)' is still TRUE and still useful — android StatsManager.as:2156 shows skill points accumulate as level-1 + DAN*(levelCap-1), so reaching 271 genuinely requires rebirths. A rewrite should replace the ledger's causal story and KEEP that parenthetical, not delete the line.

HELD, and I counted both sides myself rather than trusting the count. Web §1t1832s0§.as:2811 opens §1t2002s0§(param1:String), :2813 gets SharedObject.getLocal(cookieName + '_' + charname), :2814 clears 'saved', and :2815-2833 clear exactly NINETEEN named fields before the flush at :2836. Android QueryManagerBase.as:2936 opens deleteCharCookieData, :2940 clears 'saved', :2941-2959 clear exactly nineteen, flush at :2960. Slot-by-slot the seven unobfuscated names land in identical positions: playerLevel 4 (web :2818 / android :2944), equipment 6 (:2820/:2946), inventory 9 (:2823/:2949), stash 10 (:2824/:2950), playerlocation/taunt/friends 17-19 (:2831-2833/:2957-2959). With seven anchors in a nineteen-slot ordered list the alignment is forced. TWO CALIBRATIONS. (i) The finding's own text says 'four of which survived obfuscation ... then playerlocation, taunt, friends as the last three' — that is seven anchors described as four; sloppy wording, not a wrong claim. (ii) More importantly, the finding correctly refuses to inflate: it says only the save-format half of RR:351 falls and the server-sim-topology half still stands. I agree, and I would add one guardrail the rewrite must carry — the NINETEEN-SLOT SCHEMA is web-verified, but the twelve obfuscated field NAMES are v0.682 labels inferred by position, so they are transcribable-with-a-label, not web-attested identifiers.

new_findings.text: The ledger's own primary evidence for the stance hard-lock now argues against it, and this is decided by frames, not by code. §1t113s0§.as:326-359 is the battle HUD's third-bar updater: :328 'var _loc3_:Number = (param1 - 48) / (param2 - 48);' clamped to 0 at :329-332, :333 sets bar.scaleX, then :336-343 show a GREY getString(960) label when and only when _loc3_ == 0, :344-347 HIDE that label while 0 < _loc3_ < 1, and :348-359 swap to a BLACK getString(175) = 'Critical Hit' plus Snd_criticalDamage at _loc3_ >= 1. getString(960) is absent from the v0.682 string table (docs/gauntlet/L0/index/strings.json has no '960'), i.e. it is a web-only string. I then opened two 1080p frames and cropped x40-760, y920-1080 at 2x. reference/frames/duel_dense/Nr4fQstqHDM_428.0.png: HP 20/20 green, 26/26 blue, and a THIRD bar that is an empty brown track carrying grey text 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE', with '150% DAMAGE' (the Potato Dog buff, strings.json['4132']) below it. reference/frames/duel_frames/Nr4fQstqHDM_t435.0s.png: same player, same run, HP 19/20, and that third bar is now roughly 40% filled WHITE with NO stance text on it at all. So 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' is the Focus meter's zero-fill readout, displayed exactly while reload <= 48 — the same threshold §1t99s0§.as:3050 gates the stance cycler on — and it disappears seven seconds later in the same fight. RR:158's 'HARD-LOCKED' and RR:178's LOOK verdict describe a transient low-Focus state, not a lock. THE FRAME AND THE CODE AGREE HERE; what fails is the inference drawn from the frame.
new_findings.ledger_text: **In-combat stance is HARD-LOCKED in v0.717** ("CANNOT CHANGE STANCE"). ... Also visible: player HP **20/20**, **"150% DAMAGE"** buff (Potato Dog), **"CANNOT CHANGE STANCE"**
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 combat-core + L7 ui-hud. RR:158 and the 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' clause of RR:178 must both be rewritten, and the battle HUD gains a specified third bar: fill = (reload-48)/(maxreload-48) clamped to 0, low-end grey label at fill 0, no label mid-range, black 'Critical Hit' + Snd_criticalDamage at full.

new_findings.text: RR:195 blocker (3) 'Focus numerics (max/fill/switch-cost)' and RR:190 blocker (5) 'Focus/crit gating rule — watch the Focus bar fill/consume' both close from web source, and nobody in this packet aimed at either. CAPACITY: §1t1523s0§.as:2274-2277 is 'return 48 + (§1t7356s0§(§1t9410s0§) + §1t7358s0§(§1t9410s0§)) * 6;' with §1t9410s0§ = 8 = STAT_SPEED, i.e. maxreload = 48 + (SPD + gear SPD) * 6 — so 48 is the meter's FLOOR, which is why the stance gate and the HUD's zero point are both literally 48. REGEN: §1t99s0§.as:3318-3326 adds +6 per call, clamps to maxreload, and pushes the pair straight to the HUD updater. CONSUMPTION: §1t99s0§.as:3293-3316 zeroes the meter first if it was full (the crit spends the whole bar), then subtracts slashUsage/2 in Light, slashUsage in Balanced, slashUsage*1.5 in Heavy, clamped at 0. slashUsage is a per-weapon field with a floor of 48 (android StatsManager.as:1921-1927). That is the complete fill/consume/gate contract in one place, and it also explains the 'switch-cost' the ledger was looking for: changing stance costs nothing, it merely requires reload >= 48.

new_findings.text: RR:190 blocker (1) calls the per-stance reach cap in stage px 'the one value the whole model needs' and prescribes measuring blade-FX span off footage. It does not need measuring: it is computed, in the web build. §1t99s0§.as:3094 sets §1t4417s0§ = §1t4420s0§ * 1.4 for Light, :3105 = §1t4420s0§ * (1 + 0.2 * §1t4422s0§ * 0.1) for Balanced, :3116-3119 = §1t4420s0§ * (0.5 + 0.4 * §1t4423s0§ * 0.1) for Heavy with a hard floor of 100. The android twin names the two fields: MCSPlayer.as:97 'slashLength', :107 'baseSlashLength', same three branches at :3030/:3041/:3052-3055. baseSlashLength comes from §1t1523s0§.as:2344-2348, 'var _loc2_:int = 90 + §1t7356s0§(§1t9426s0§) * 5; return int(120 + Math.floor(_loc2_ * param1 / (20 + param1)));' with param1 = SPD (x1.5 under the speed buff, :2336-2341) and §1t9426s0§ = STAT_DAN. And slashLength is spent as a LENGTH BUDGET on the drawn blade path, not a hitbox radius: android InputManager.as:51 'maxDistance:int = 200', :106-109 setMaxDistance, :198 'distanceLeft = maxDistance', :360 tapers the stroke as (maxDistance - distanceLeft)/maxDistance. So at dan 0 the base runs 120 px (SPD 0) asymptotically to 210 px, giving Light 168-294 px, Balanced 120-252 px, Heavy max(100, 60-189) px, and every rebirth raises the asymptote by 5 px.

new_findings.text: RR:161-163 item 3 tells the next build session to 'either model the mastery curve or decide-and-flag "the build targets mastery-9"'. The curve is in the payload, it is linear, and it reproduces BOTH ends of the ledger's own table. §1t99s0§.as:3258-3271: base = minDamage + Math.random() * damageRange; Light = base * (0.5 + 0.4 * lightMastery * 0.1); Balanced = base * (1 + 0.2 * balancedMastery * 0.1); Heavy, Dual and Reversed all = base * 1.4 flat. At mastery 0 that is exactly the ledger's level-1 Shugyosha row 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.4; at mastery 10 it is exactly the ledger's ceiling row 0.9 / 1.2 / 1.4. The identical shape governs reach (0.5 + 0.04m for Heavy, 1 + 0.02m for Balanced, flat 1.4 for Light), so one linear rule covers both tables. This CONFIRMS the ledger's item 3 rather than overturning it, but it removes the fork: model the curve, do not flag a mastery-9 target. Build divergence to respect: android MCSPlayer.as:3205-3213 uses 0.5 + 0.5*m*0.01 and 1 + 0.5*m*0.01 on a 0-100 mastery scale with Heavy at 1.5, so the android coefficients must not be ported.
new_findings.quote: §1t99s0§.as:3262 '_loc2_ = _loc1_ * (0.5 + 0.4 * this.§1t4421s0§ * 0.1);' :3265 '_loc2_ = _loc1_ * (1 + 0.2 * this.§1t4422s0§ * 0.1);' :3270 '_loc2_ = _loc1_ * 1.4;' ‖ android MCSPlayer.as:3205 'maxDamage = baseDamage * (0.5 + 0.5 * this.lightMastery * 0.01);' :3213 'maxDamage = baseDamage * 1.5;'
new_findings.ledger_text: 3. **The stance tables (dmg 0.9/1.2/1.4, reach 300/200/100) are MASTERY-9 CEILING values, not base.** ... → Either model the mastery curve or **decide-and-flag "the build targets mastery-9"** and label accordingly.
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 combat-core. Item 3 is upheld and upgraded: the curve is dmgMult(Light)=0.5+0.04m, dmgMult(Balanced)=1+0.02m, dmgMult(Heavy)=1.4, m in 0..10 — CONTRACT from web source. The decide-and-flag branch can be deleted.

new_findings.text: RR:195 blocker (4) 'SPD->cooldown formula' and the cooldown half of RR:200 blocker (1) 'SPD range/cooldown scaling (wiki gives only direction)' both close from the web payload. §1t1523s0§.as:2289-2296 is 'internal static function §1t9590s0§(param1:int) : Number { if(param1 > 600) { param1 = 600; } return 1 - param1 / 600 * 0.5; }', fed by :2279-2287 which reads STAT_SPEED plus gear bonus and multiplies by 1.5 while the speed buff is active. So the cooldown multiplier is 1 - min(SPD_effective, 600)/600 * 0.5, i.e. a linear ramp from 1.0x down to a hard floor of 0.5x at SPD 600. THIS IS A BUILD DIVERGENCE AND IT MATTERS: android StatsManager.as:1854-1860 caps at 300, not 600, so the mobile build halves cooldowns at half the stat. A recreation targeting v0.717 must take 600.
new_findings.ledger_text: ④ SPD→cooldown formula. ... ① DEF mitigation curve + SPD range/cooldown scaling (wiki gives only direction) — *measure per-point deltas in a build.*
new_findings.lane_impact: L2 skills-meters blocker (4) closes as CONTRACT; L4 progression blocker (1) loses its cooldown half (the DEF-mitigation half survives). Config: SKILL_CD_MULT = 1 - min(SPD,600)/600*0.5.

new_findings.text: RR:245 blocker (3) files 'Dan-rank count/titles (garbled source)' as a naming problem. It is also a BALANCE problem the ledger never noticed: dan rank feeds the reach formula. §1t1523s0§.as:2346 computes the reach asymptote as 'var _loc2_:int = 90 + §1t7356s0§(§1t9426s0§) * 5;' with §1t9426s0§ = 25 = STAT_DAN (android StatsManager.as:220), so every rebirth adds 5 px to the maximum blade-path length — 90 at dan 0 rising to 135 at the dan-9 cap, i.e. a base reach asymptote of 210 px climbing to 255 px. The titles themselves are also fully resolved and there are TEN of them, ids 455 through 464 in the string table: (初段)(弐段)(参段)(四段)(五段)(六段)(七段)(八段)(九段)(十段), which matches the '< 9' hard cap in the rebirth routine exactly. Parity note: the titles are read from the v0.682 table, so they carry the S0-3 UI-copy caveat; the 90 + DAN*5 formula does not, it is web source.
